text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- NEW TAX WILL COST STATES 9 BLN REAIS

The central government should raise around 9 billion reais from state and municipal governments with the new Fiscal Stability Fund (FEF) which will replace the Emergency Social Fund (FSE) under a new constitutional amendment which is scheduled to sent to Congress.
Banco Excel Economico has raised $150 million with an eight year bond in its first international issue Banco Economico was bought out last year.
-- TELEBRAS: A BATTLE BETWEEN 80 AND 84 REAIS

Today's stock market options settlement should not produce any surprises. Pressure from investors, intent on pushing up the Telebras price, increased the stock's price by 0.5 percent to 82.70 reais which means the option will almost certainly settle at 80.00 reais.
-- SOLUTION TO RIO'S CELL PHONES ONLY IN 1997

The long-suffering users of Rio de Janeiro's cell phone system, who routinely endure interruptions, dialing headaches and incomplete calls, will have to wait until next year for a permanent solution to these problems, Telerj officials said.
-- STRAY BULLET WOUNDS 9 MO BABY AT THE CIRCUS
A nine month old baby was wounded in the arm by a stray bullet that hit him while he was being held by his father at the circus. The baby, who was rushed to the hospital, is out of danger.
-- GOVERNMENT TO EXPEL MINERS FROM SERRA PELADA MINE

The Federal Government is working on a plan to expel close to 2,000 miners that are ilegaly installed at the Serra Pelada gold mine. Once again last week, the miners prevented officials from state mining company Vale do Rio Doce from working in the mine.
-- JORGE AMADO TO BE OPERATED TODAY
Jorge Amado, Brazil's most widely read author, will go into surgery today to have a heart artery unplugged.
